rationale: previous-feedback.txt contains no failure to repair: trial-a9f72afa23 was accepted (decision.accepted=true, objective 3.4017685 ms vs paired parent 3.6846775, quality pass at max_abs_error 9.5e-6 with exact top1, coverage 2/2 on f2cf62caf57ad09f5d2f36aa, no fallbacks), so this attempt composes on the installed whole-bundle replacement of group eca3643289778aea5af3 by explicitly replacing bundle trial-a9f72afa23-param-f2e37a0c and re-owning its entire behavior at module call f2cf62caf57ad09f5d2f36aa: eval BatchNorm2d folded into bias-free conv weights at build time, fused residual add+bias+ReLU and conv bias+ReLU Triton epilogues, identical aten conv2d/adaptive_avg_pool2d/linear ops under the frozen FP32/no-TF32/cudnn.benchmark=False policy, the lazy side-stream warmup -> CUDA-graph capture -> replay-verified-at-1e-4 flow with input-signature (shape/stride/dtype/device/data_ptr) guards, the eager fused path, and parent fallback for unsupported signatures. The accepted revision's own evidence (nsys execution_timeline: 59 kernels, active union 3335.81us, 2.85us inter-kernel gaps; cProfile host side = one graph replay 0.040ms + 3.19ms synchronize wait) shows launch headroom is exhausted, so this increment attacks GPU kernel time only, with four changes inside the existing capture/warmup/verified-replay flow: (1) a fused Triton shortcut epilogue per downsample stage computing relu(conv2_out + 1x1/stride-2 projection(x) + bsum) with the K=64/128/256 projection accumulated in-register via tl.dot(input_precision='ieee') tiles (128x64 tile, BLOCK_K=64), deleting the sres tensor that the accepted path writes with implicit_convolve_sgemm (measured 48.4/17.9/22.0us) and re-reads with _add_bias_relu (9.8/7.5/11.7us) plus three computeOffsetsKernel (~3.5us total) - 120.1us measured for ~26/13/7us of unique bytes at ~2TB/s; (2) a Triton implicit-GEMM conv+bias+ReLU (tl.dot ieee, K=2304 exact, 128x64 tiles, 100 CTAs) for layer4 block1 conv1 3x3/stride-2 256->512 whose 7x7 output grid cudnn tile-quantizes (_5x_cudnn_ampere_scudnn_128x64_relu_small_nn_v1 grid 13x8, 152.9us at 24.2 TF/s, plus 9.4us _bias_relu); (3) a Triton implicit-GEMM replacement for the stem 7x7/stride-2 conv (_5x_cudnn_ampere_scudnn_128x64_relu_medium_nn_v1 257.7us at 29.3 TF/s effective) feeding the unchanged fused pool epilogue; (4) a retiled _bias_relu_pool kernel with cross-row register reuse (R=8 output rows per program, rolling window rows) replacing the accepted one-row-per-program kernel that measured 124.7us at ~1.03TB/s while neighboring pointwise kernels reach ~2.1-2.6TB/s. Host-side index math for all four kernels was validated on CPU (fp64 gather emulation matches aten conv2d exactly, incl. odd sizes; the pool kernel is bitwise-equal to relu(maxpool(x)+b) on five shapes) and all six Triton kernels ahead-of-time compile for sm90 in the worker's Triton 3.7.1. Expected benefit is the selection's hypothesis (~0.15-0.25ms, target ~3.15-3.25ms vs accepted 3.4017685, noise bounds 0.013-0.019ms), decided by measured AB/BA timing, not these estimates. The layer1 direct convs (33 TF/s), the nine winograd s1 convs, the classifier GEMM, workload, batch=32, FP32 IEEE precision, measurement boundaries and quality checks stay untouched; the three observed descendant calls (enter hook 4aab5013037467cf91b2a114, exit hook 82be0731963c69a18149b577, logits clone 9b2f8fbe19d203f9499fe887 on the replay path) are re-emitted each invocation exactly as in the accepted lineage. Every new kernel is individually guarded (exact geometry/stride/padding/dilation/groups/channel/contiguity/dtype checks, per-kernel broken latches, capture-time exceptions re-raised so the graph is dropped instead of producing wrong output) and falls back to the accepted bundle's bitwise aten path; the retained graph_logits.clone() keeps the observed aten.clone call site. Route labels (captured, cuda_graph_replay, eager_fused_v3, capture_failed, capture_verification_failed, graph_replay_failed, parent_fallback_unsupported_signature, setup_failure:*) are diagnostic self-report only.

setup_work.parameter_transform: At build time (torch.inference_mode(False), torch.no_grad(), unchanged from the accepted bundle): fold the 20 eval BatchNorm2d affines (gamma/sqrt(var+eps), beta-mean*scale) into contiguous FP32 conv-weight copies (~44.7MB, convs stay bias-free so cudnn heuristics see identical shapes), per-channel biases with the shortcut bias pre-added per basic layer (bsum), and clone the detached classifier weight/bias (~2.1MB). The new kernels add no persistent tensors: the (Cout,Cin) projection view, (64,147) stem view and (512,2304) conv1 view are zero-copy views of the already-folded weights. Original parameters are untouched, so parent fallback and framework restore keep exact parent semantics.
setup_work.first_cuda_invocation: Unchanged from the accepted bundle, now covering six Triton kernels (_bias_relu, _add_bias_relu, the retiled _bias_relu_pool_rows, _conv7x7s2, _conv3x3s2, _proj_add): Triton JIT compile on the first eager fused call inside the adapter's real forward/inference_mode context, then side-stream warmup, CUDA-graph capture of the fused static sequence, and a replay-vs-eager verification at atol=rtol=1e-4 before the graph is used - all on the first candidate CUDA call, which precedes the timed repeats (warmup=2, quality checks first); later timed invocations replay. Any kernel compile/launch failure outside capture latches only that kernel's broken flag onto the accepted bitwise aten path; during capture the exception disables the graph, never the output.
setup_work.memory: Setup allocates ~46.8MB of folded/cloned FP32 parameters that stay alive for the warm-model lifecycle (same as the accepted bundle; the new kernels add views only). The CUDA graph retains a private pool roughly the size of the activation high-water mark, increasing reserved/lifecycle_reserved bytes - an allocator-scope effect, not a physical-memory saving; none of the PyTorch counters measures the graph pool's reserved bytes as allocated. The stem conv still materializes its 32x64x112x112 output (205.5MB) between the conv and pool kernels as in the accepted bundle, but the three downsample stages no longer write/re-read sres tensors (12.8/6.4/3.2MB), so per-run peak_allocated_bytes is expected to stay at or slightly below the accepted ~141.1MB; framework.lifecycle_peak_allocated_bytes (~260.9MB observed) and lifecycle_peak_reserved_bytes continue to include preparation/installation plus the graph pool.

quality_risks: The four replaced GPU pieces reassociate FP32 accumulation order only (tl.dot input_precision='ieee' gives exact FMA semantics; no TF32 anywhere). Per-element sums change only inside the replaced kernels - the same reassociation class the accepted bundle already shipped at measured max_abs_error 9.5e-6 vs the eager parent, under atol=rtol=1e-4; exact top1 can only flip if two classes are nearly tied in the reference.

Index math was validated by fp64 gather emulation against aten conv2d (exact, incl. odd spatial sizes and border/padding lanes) and the pool kernel is bitwise-identical to the accepted relu(maxpool(x)+b) on five shapes; remaining risk is Triton codegen/runtime behavior on the leased GPU, covered by per-kernel guards that latch to the accepted bitwise aten path on any launch exception (capture-time exceptions disable the graph instead of producing wrong output).
Triton maximum drops NaN where aten propagates it; the frozen fixture and weights are finite, so no NaN is expected on this path (same caveat as the accepted bundle's pointwise kernels).

Fusion guards accept only the exact observed geometries (MaxPool2d k3/s2/p1/d1/ceil=False stem pool; 7x7/s2/p3 stem conv 3->64; 3x3/s2/p1 256->512 for layer4 block1 conv1; 1x1/s2/p0 shortcut projections with channel multiples of 128/64). Every other geometry, non-contiguous input, wrong dtype or Triton failure keeps the accepted bundle's separate-kernel sequence bitwise.

CUDA graph capture/replay can fail on unusual worker states; every graph step stays guarded (capture_failed, capture_verification_failed, graph_replay_failed labels) and degrades to the eager fused path, never to wrong output. The graph reads the live input storage, so mutated input contents are recomputed on each replay; different tensor objects with non-matching signatures take the eager path. If the evaluator rebuilds the input tensor per invocation (different data_ptr), the guard routes every call to the eager fused path: still correct, with all fused-kernel savings except replay.

Graph replay does not re-execute the parent's inner Python calls; the earlier whole bundle is explicitly replaced and eliminated_calls lists every descendant again, with equivalent conv/pool/linear work continuing inside the replacement. Route labels are candidate telemetry, not independent proof; the framework's output checks, coverage counters and nsys traces remain the accepting evidence.

Performance risk, not correctness: the Triton conv replacements are hypotheses from measured cudnn inefficiencies (24.2-29.3 TF/s effective on the replaced convs); if a replacement runs slower than its cudnn counterpart on the leased H100-class device, the candidate only loses the paired AB/BA measurement - quality and guards are unaffected, and the accepted bundle stays installed on rejection.
